title: Maki roll
transcript:
[PLACEHOLDER NARRATION — replace with the real chef transcript]
Today we're making a simple maki roll, and I'll show you exactly what it should look like at every step. First, lay a sheet of nori on the bamboo mat, shiny side down, with the long edge towards you. The rough side holds the rice. Next, dip your fingers in the water bowl and shake off the excess. You wet your hands so the rice doesn't stick to your fingers and you can spread it gently without squashing the grains. Now take a small handful of rice and spread it in a thin, even layer. You should still see the dark nori through the rice in places. Leave about two centimetres of bare nori along the far edge, because that strip seals the roll. Most beginners use far too much rice, and then the roll won't close. Lay one line of filling across the third of the sheet closest to you. Just one thin line of cucumber; don't pile it up, or it squeezes out when you roll. To roll, lift the near edge of the mat, tuck the nori over the filling, then roll forward and press gently along the whole length so it holds its shape. Finally, wet your knife, cut the roll in half, then cut each half into three equal pieces. Six even pieces, and you're done.

steps.title: Place nori
steps.key_line: Shiny side down, long edge near
steps.instruction: Lay a sheet of nori on the bamboo mat, shiny side down, with the long edge towards you.
steps.chef_quote: Lay a sheet of nori on the bamboo mat, shiny side down, with the long edge towards you.
success_criteria: One whole nori sheet lies flat on the mat
The long edge of the sheet faces the cook

watch_fors.mistake: The nori is turned so its short edge faces the cook
watch_fors.headline: Turn the nori
watch_fors.spoken: Turn the nori so the long edge is towards you.

steps.title: Wet hands
steps.key_line: Dip fingers, shake off the excess
steps.instruction: Dip your fingers in the water bowl and shake off the excess so the rice doesn't stick.
steps.chef_quote: You wet your hands so the rice doesn't stick to your fingers.
success_criteria: The nori sheet is still dry and flat on the mat

steps.title: Spread rice
steps.instruction: Spread a small handful of rice in a thin, even layer, leaving about two centimetres of bare nori along the far edge.
steps.chef_quote: You should still see the dark nori through the rice in places.
success_criteria: Rice layer is thin enough to see nori through it in places
A strip of bare nori about 2 cm wide remains along the far edge
Rice covers the rest of the sheet evenly, without bare patches

watch_fors.mistake: Rice layer is thick and covers the whole sheet
watch_fors.headline: Too much rice
watch_fors.spoken: There's a bit too much rice — spread it thinner and leave two centimetres of nori at the top.

watch_fors.mistake: Rice reaches the far edge, leaving no bare nori strip
watch_fors.headline: No top margin
watch_fors.spoken: Push the rice back so there's a two-centimetre strip of bare nori at the far edge.

steps.title: Add fillings
steps.key_line: One line across the near third
steps.instruction: Lay one thin line of filling across the third of the sheet closest to you.
steps.chef_quote: Just one thin line of cucumber; don't pile it up.
success_criteria: Filling forms a single thin line running across the sheet
The line sits in the third of the sheet nearest the cook

watch_fors.mistake: Filling is piled high or spread over more than one line
watch_fors.headline: Too much filling
watch_fors.spoken: That's a lot of filling — keep it to one thin line so the roll closes.

steps.title: Roll
steps.instruction: Lift the near edge of the mat, tuck the nori over the filling, then roll forward and press gently along the whole length.
steps.chef_quote: Press gently along the whole length so it holds its shape.
success_criteria: The roll is closed, with the bare nori strip sealed underneath
The roll has an even thickness along its length

steps.title: Slice
steps.instruction: Wet your knife, cut the roll in half, then cut each half into three equal pieces.
steps.chef_quote: Six even pieces, and you're done.
success_criteria: There are six pieces of roughly equal width
Each piece shows the filling in the centre
